name: DeepSeek
intro: DeepSeek — the Hangzhou lab behind the R1 shock of January 2025 — generated $70M+ of revenue in the first seven months of 2026, roughly 10x all of 2025, putting its annualized run rate near $500M with API prices a fraction of US frontier labs. Every reported figure is collected below, each traced back to a public source; no audited financials have been published.

milestones.note: A research lab first: annualized revenue estimated in the single-digit millions, with the chatbot free and API priced near cost.

milestones.label: Jan '25
milestones.note: The R1 release makes DeepSeek a household name; the app tops US app stores and API sign-ups surge, with one reported service outage day generating notable revenue spikes.

milestones.label: Dec '25
milestones.note: Sacra estimates just $12M annualized at end-2025 — surprisingly small given the fame, reflecting aggressively subsidized pricing.

milestones.label: Mid '26
milestones.note: $70–71M of revenue booked in ~7 months — roughly 10x all of 2025 — with 70–80% gross margins as the price subsidies eased.

milestones.label: Aug '26
milestones.note: Sacra estimates ~$500M annualized; reports describe a ~$1.5B raise in talks and IPO preparations targeting 2027, or possibly late 2026.

modelParagraphs: DeepSeek monetizes almost entirely through usage-based API billing, priced dramatically below US frontier labs — historically around 30x cheaper than OpenAI on comparable workloads, with chat free on web and mobile. The strategy was deliberately to subsidize price to win developers; as subsidies eased through 2026, reported gross margins ran at 70–80%, unusually strong for a lab competing on cost.

There are no subscriptions and no enterprise salesforce — the revenue is raw token volume at extreme efficiency, enabled by in-house infrastructure and training-cost innovations. That is also why revenue stayed tiny (est. ~$12M annualized at end-2025) even after R1 made the brand globally famous, and why it then compounded ~10x in seven months once pricing normalized.
revenueMix: Token billing priced ~30x below US frontier labs; the entire business.
Consumer app generates no direct revenue — it is the distribution engine.
No subscriptions or enterprise contracts reported to date.

faqs.a: Sacra estimates DeepSeek hit ~$500 million in annualized revenue by August 2026, up from just ~$12M at the end of 2025. Reported booked revenue of $70–71M in the first seven months of 2026 — about 10x all of 2025 — supports the run-rate estimate. No audited financials have been published.

Almost entirely usage-based API billing, priced roughly 30x below OpenAI on comparable workloads, with the consumer chatbot free. There is no subscription tier and no reported enterprise sales motion.

Reportedly close to it — press reports cite 70–80% gross margins on API revenue as of 2026, a function of extreme infrastructure efficiency rather than premium pricing. Audited figures do not exist publicly.

Reports describe a ~$1.5 billion raise in talks at valuations from roughly $71B to $74B — a ~7x jump in four months. These rest on unverified revenue estimates; analysts caution no audited financials back them.

Reports indicate DeepSeek is preparing an IPO filing, with a listing targeted for 2027 or possibly as early as late 2026, alongside its first external capital raise — a shift from pure research lab to commercial company.
